haiku-low.q1: Order (status PENDING) and an OrderPlaced outbox row, in one transaction. Customer gets 202 with the orderId before any other service acts.
haiku-low.q2: Only after the broker acks the publish. A crash between ack and marking republishes the row, so delivery is at-least-once.
haiku-low.q3: The topic is keyed by orderId, which gives per-order ordering within each consumer group.
haiku-low.q4: A StockReserved event triggers the charge; Payment ignores OrderPlaced. StockSvc emits StockReserved only after its hold commits, so no charge without stock.
haiku-low.q5: Via a per-service outbox written in the same transaction as the state change. After a crash, the unsent row goes out on the next poll.
haiku-low.q6: It checks a dedupe table keyed on eventId first and skips if present; otherwise it inserts the eventId in the same transaction as its side effect.
haiku-low.q7: PaySvc always sends orderId as the idempotency key, so the retried charge call returns the original capture instead of charging again.
haiku-low.q8: A decline is a normal PaymentDeclined path (hold released, order cancelled). A timeout or 5xx throws and goes through retries, then the DLQ.
haiku-low.q9: A PaymentDeclined event. StockSvc releases the hold in its stock DB, then records the event as seen.
haiku-low.q10: It consumes StockUnavailable, PaymentCaptured or PaymentDeclined. If still PENDING, it sets CONFIRMED or CANCELLED plus an outbox event, in one transaction.
haiku-low.q11: OrderConfirmed or OrderCancelled events from the bus. A failed send throws into normal retries and DLQ; the order status is never touched.
haiku-low.q12: Four tries total, 1s, 10s and 60s apart. Then the message goes to the group's DLQ, on-call is paged, and the order keeps its status.

sonnet.q1: The order (status PENDING) plus an OrderPlaced outbox row, written in one transaction. The customer gets 202 with the orderId; the handler publishes nothing itself.
sonnet.q2: A row is marked sent only after the broker's ack. If the relay crashes after the ack but before marking, the row is republished (duplicate, at-least-once).
sonnet.q3: All events are on the order-events topic keyed by orderId, which gives per-order ordering within each consumer group.
sonnet.q4: PaySvc charges on a StockReserved event (it ignores OrderPlaced). StockSvc only emits StockReserved after the hold commits, so no charge happens without stock.
sonnet.q5: Each writes its state change and an outbox row in the same transaction, and a relay publishes the row to the bus. If it crashes after commit but before publishing, nothing is lost: the row is still unsent and goes out on the first poll after restart.
sonnet.q6: Each consumer has its own consumer group and a dedupe table keyed on eventId in its own DB. It looks up the eventId first; if it is present it acks and skips. Otherwise it inserts the eventId in the same transaction as the side effect and outbox row, commits, then acks. The PK catches two copies racing.
sonnet.q7: PaySvc always sends orderId as the idempotency key to the card provider. The redelivered StockReserved isn't in the seen table, so the charge is called again with the same key and returns the original capture. Then the commit goes through.
sonnet.q8: A decline is not an error: it becomes a PaymentDeclined event, StockSvc releases the hold and OMS cancels. A card provider timeout or 5xx is an error (a throw) and goes through retries and then the DLQ.
sonnet.q9: The PaymentDeclined event, consumed by StockSvc, which releases the hold (release + seen).
sonnet.q10: OrderSvc/OMS consumes StockUnavailable, PaymentCaptured or PaymentDeclined. Only if the order is still PENDING, it sets status to CONFIRMED or CANCELLED, with an OrderConfirmed/OrderCancelled outbox row and a dedupe (seen) insert, all in one transaction.
sonnet.q11: The Mailer consuming OrderConfirmed or OrderCancelled from the bus triggers the email. If the send fails, it throws and goes through normal retries and the DLQ. The order status is unaffected, since the Mailer never touches order status.
sonnet.q12: Four tries in total, with retries after 1 s, 10 s and 60 s. Then the message goes to the DLQ for that consumer group, on-call is paged, and the consumer carries on with the next message. Nothing is rolled back and the order stays in its current status (e.g. PENDING with the stock hold still in place if PaySvc dead-lettered).
